questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, what must you do?

options.text: Let other traffic pass if they are close enough to cause a crash.
Let only vehicles on your right pass.
Always slow down but keep moving without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass if they are close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Let any crossing or merging traffic pass, especially traffic close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often, to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To check if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often, to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors often so you know where vehicles are near you. Do not stare at one spot for too long.

questions.question: You are driving in the far right lane of a four-lane freeway and see thick broken white lines on the left side of your lane. What lane are you in?

options.text: The carpool lane and must move to another lane.
A special lane for slow-moving vehicles.
An exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: An exit lane.
questions.explanation: Thick broken white lines on a freeway show that the lane is ending. Be ready to exit or for the lane to merge.

questions.question: Which is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using your high beam lights in fog.
Staring straight ahead at the road.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors every two to five seconds to see hazards. Staring only ahead is unsafe. In fog, use low beam lights, not high beams.

questions.question: You arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles to your right and left. What should you do?

options.text: Let the vehicle on your left go first.
Let the vehicle on your right go first.
Wait until all vehicles are gone before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on your right has the right-of-way. Then vehicles go in the order they arrived.

questions.question: What is true about vehicles with a diamond-shaped hazardous load sign?

options.text: They cannot drive on freeways.
They must stop before crossing railroad tracks.
They cannot drive faster than 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must stop before crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous loads must stop before crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: In rainy weather, when should you be most careful while turning or stopping?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
Half an hour after the rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars mixes with rain and makes the road slippery.

questions.question: What describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: Other drivers will do the right thing.
They expect other drivers might make mistakes and are ready to react.
They expect no help and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They expect other drivers might make mistakes and are ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting other drivers to make errors and being prepared to respond safely.

questions.question: When is it illegal to enter an intersection?

options.text: When you cannot cross completely before the light turns red.
When the light is flashing yellow and you did not stop first.
When the light is yellow and you cannot stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you cannot cross completely before the light turns red.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can get all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: What must you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
Slow down and proceed carefully.
Stop completely and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians pass, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a white painted curb mean?

options.text: Loading zone for freight or passengers.
Loading zone for passengers or mail only.
Loading zone for freight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loading zone for passengers or mail only.
questions.explanation: At a white curb, you can stop only to pick up or drop off passengers or mail.

questions.question: What speed should you drive when merging onto a freeway?

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
The posted freeway speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging onto a freeway, match the speed of traffic around you.

questions.question: When planning to pass another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Do not count on other drivers to make room for you.
Assume the driver will let you pass if you use your signal.
Assume the driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not count on other drivers to make room for you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will help you pass or that you have enough time to pass multiple vehicles. You can return to your lane when you see both headlights of the other vehicle in your mirror.

questions.question: If your vehicle is about to be hit from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing into your seat and against the head restraint. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake. What should you do with the front wheels?

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Leave the front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or road edge.

questions.question: You see heavy smoke covering the road ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
Slow down, move right, and stop off the roadway.
Turn on high beam headlights and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move right, and stop off the roadway.
questions.explanation: If you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down right away. Move as far right as possible and stop off the roadway. Then check if it is safe to continue. Heavy smoke can irritate your eyes and lungs or be dangerous.

questions.question: You want to enter the freeway but don't see a gap in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap. Do not stop at the end of the ramp. You need space to speed up to match traffic before entering the freeway.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light pointing right means you:

options.text: May turn after slowing and checking for traffic.
Cannot turn until the light turns green.
May turn after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Never turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, you should use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit and the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and go through without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means caution. The light will soon turn red. Stop at a yellow light if you can do so safely. Otherwise, cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: When can minors use a cell phone without a hands-free device while driving?

options.text: When making a call at a red light
When calling for emergency help
Never

questions.correctAnswerText: When calling for emergency help
questions.explanation: Minors cannot use a cell phone while driving, except to call for emergency help. Adult drivers may use hands-free devices but should only make calls if needed for emergencies.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, you must:

options.text: Yield to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic that is close enough to cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, let traffic in the lanes you want to enter go first. Be ready to stop, but you may go if there is no traffic coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The height distance from the road to a bridge or overpass.
The maximum height of a vehicle allowed in this state.
The maximum width of a vehicle allowed on the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The height distance from the road to a bridge or overpass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of low clearance. It shows the distance from the road surface to the bottom of a bridge or overpass (in this case, 12 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: California's "Basic Speed Law" requires you to:

options.text: Drive at the same speed as other traffic.
Never drive faster than is safe for current conditions.
Always drive at the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never drive faster than is safe for current conditions.
questions.explanation: The "Basic Speed Law" says you cannot drive faster than conditions allow. For example, driving 45 mph in a 55 mph zone during heavy fog may still be too fast for those conditions.

questions.question: When a traffic signal light is not working, you must:

options.text: Stop, then go when it is safe.
Stop and let all other traffic go first.
Slow down or stop only if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: When a traffic signal is broken and has no lights, treat the intersection as if all directions have stop signs.

questions.question: To avoid glare from oncoming headlights, you should:

options.text: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
Keep looking at the center line of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid bright oncoming lights. Then continue watching ahead to see where the other vehicle is.

questions.question: If your vehicle is about to be hit from the rear, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If hit from the rear, press yourself against your seat and head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your freeway lane. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
Speed up to protect your right-of-way.
Always keep your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if you can.
questions.explanation: When safe, make room for vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Braking makes the skid worse.
